gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text: Gross profit in the first quarter of 2025 increased $11 million, or 1% on a reported basis, to $1.035 billion (36.4% of sales) compared to $1,024 million (35.3% of sales) in the 2024 period. The increase in gross profit was primarily driven by volume increases and productivity gains, offset in part by the effect of exchange rate variations and the net impact of the change in business portfolio mix due to divestitures of $21 million.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales
cor.text: Cost of sales decreased $67 million to $1.808 billion (63.6% of sales) in the first quarter of 2025 compared to $1.875 billion (64.7% of sales) in the first quarter of 2024. The decrease in cost of goods sold was primarily driven by lower raw material costs and manufacturing expenses, lower unfavorable manufacturing absorption compared to the prior year period and the change in business portfolio mix due to divestitures, with an impact of approximately $10 million, offset in part by volume increases in sales.

rd.heading: Research and Development (R&D) Expenses
rd.text: R&D expenses decreased $2 million to $164 million (5.8% of sales) in the first quarter of 2025 compared to $166 million (5.7% of sales) in the first quarter of 2024. The decrease in R&D expenses was primarily driven by lower operating expenses for R&D related activities.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense decreased to $71 million in the first quarter of 2025 compared to $83 million in the first quarter of 2024. The decrease in interest expense was primarily due to debt repayments at maturity made during the three months ended March 31, 2024, related to the 2024 Term Loan Facility and 2024 Euro Notes. See Note 13 for additional information.

gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text: Gross profit in 2024 increased $443 million, or 12% on a reported basis, to $4.124 billion (35.9% of sales) compared to $3.681 billion (32.1% of sales) in the 2023 period. The increase in gross profit was primarily driven by volume increases and productivity gains, offset in part by the effect of exchange rate variations and the net impact of the change in business portfolio mix due to divestitures of $133 million.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales
cor.text: Cost of sales decreased $438 million to $7.360 billion (64.1% of sales) in 2024 compared to $7.798 billion (67.9% of sales) in 2023. The decrease in cost of sales was primarily driven by the change in business portfolio mix due to divestitures which was approximately $227 million, lower raw material costs and manufacturing expenses, lower unfavorable manufacturing absorption compared to the prior year period, increased productivity compared to the prior year period, offset in part by volume increases.

rd.heading: Research and Development (R&D) Expenses
rd.text: R&D expenses increased $35 million to $671 million (5.8% of sales) in 2024 compared to $636 million (5.5% of sales) in 2023. The increase in R&D expenses was primarily driven by an increase in incentive compensation expense, offset in part by the net impact of the change in business portfolio mix due to divestitures and the effect of exchange rate variations.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense decreased $75 million to $305 million in 2024 compared to $380 million in 2023. The decrease in interest expense was due to lower debt outstanding. See Note 14 for additional information.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: The effective tax rate in 2024 was 11.2% compared to (1.8)% in 2023. The year-over-year increase was primarily driven by an increase in pre-tax income, changes in the mix of earnings, the tax impact of business divestitures and certain non-recurring tax benefits. See Note 10 for additional information.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows Provided By Operating Activities
ocf.text: Cash flows provided by operating activities in 2024 were $1.070 billion, or 9.3% of sales, compared to $1.439 billion, or 12.5% of sales, in 2023. The decrease in cash flows from operating activities from 2023 to 2024 was primarily driven by an increase in working capital, largely related to trade receivables and inventories including amounts held for sale, offset in part by accounts payable and higher cash earnings, excluding the impact of non-cash adjustments.

gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text: Gross profit in 2025 decreased $186 million, or 5% on a reported basis, to $3.938 billion (36.2% of sales) from $4.124 billion (35.9% of sales) in the 2024 period. The decrease in gross profit was primarily driven by the impact of divestitures of $264 million and the effect of exchange rate variations, offset in part by volume increases and productivity gains.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales
cor.text: Cost of sales decreased $408 million to $6.952 billion (63.8% of sales) in 2025 compared to $7.360 billion (64.1% of sales) in 2024. The decrease in cost of sales was primarily driven by the divestitures the impact of which was approximately $493 million, lower raw material costs and lower unfavorable manufacturing absorption compared to the prior year period, increased productivity compared to the prior year period, offset in part by volume increases. With the decrease in cost of sales, gross margin increased, reflecting the benefit of lower costs and improved productivity.

rd.heading: Research and Development (“R&D”) Expenses
rd.text: R&D expenses increased $23 million to $694 million (6.4% of sales) in 2025 compared to $671 million (5.8% of sales) in 2024. The increase in R&D expenses was primarily driven by an increase in employee related costs and operating expenses for R&D related activities, offset in part by the impact of the divestitures and the effect of exchange rate variations.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense decreased $76 million to $229 million in 2025 compared to $305 million in 2024. The decrease in interest expense was due to lower debt outstanding. See Note 14 for additional information.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: The effective tax rate in 2025 was 12.9% compared to 13.3% in 2024. The year-over-year decrease was primarily driven by the tax benefit resulting from the entity realignment project, offset in part by the impact of business divestitures, tax effects of non-deductible goodwill impairment and changes in the mix of earnings post-divestitures. See Note 10 for additional information.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows Provided By Operating Activities
ocf.text: Cash flows provided by operating activities in 2025 were $850 million, or 7.8% of sales, compared to $1.070 billion, or 9.3% of sales, in 2024. The decrease in cash flows from operating activities from 2024 to 2025 was primarily driven by an increase in working capital and a larger incentive compensation payout made in 2025 related to 2024 results, offset in part by an increase in accounts receivables in the prior year.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Our business is geographically diverse, with sales in the U.S. representing approximately 28% of sales in 2025.
In 2025, no customer accounted for 10% or more of sales.
In 2025, our 25 largest customers, a majority of which were multinational consumer products companies, collectively accounted for approximately 32% of our sales.
In 2025, approximately 72% of our combined net sales were to customers outside the U.S., and we intend to continue expansion of our international operations.
The Company had no customers that accounted for greater than 10 % of consolidated net sales in 2025, 2024 and 2023.
The Company had no customer that accounted for more than 10 % of its consolidated net sales for the years ended 2025, 2024 and 2023.
Our products rely on both natural and synthetic ingredients.
Revenue from collaborations depends on our partners’ performance, and these arrangements may not lead to timely or successful product development or commercialization.
For certain materials, we rely on a limited number of suppliers or regions, making us vulnerable to shortages, delays, and price volatility.
Dividends are authorized and determined by our Board of Directors in its sole discretion and depend upon a number of factors, including:
We rely on patents, trademarks, copyrights and trade secrets to protect our intellectual property rights.

We often rely on trade secrets to protect our products, manufacturing processes, extract methodologies and other processes, as this does not require us to publicly file information regarding our intellectual property.

While we have historically paid dividends on a quarterly basis to shareholders of our common stock, the declaration and payment of future dividends will depend on many factors, including, but not limited to, our earnings, financial condition, business development needs and regulatory considerations.
Operating cash flow provides the primary source of funds for capital investment needs, dividends paid to shareholders, treasury share repurchases and debt service repayments.
